page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a fourth-generation compute-optimized virtual machine running on the Xen hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 25 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, requiring all persistent storage workloads to rely on remote Elastic Block Store volumes over its 5 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark testing situates the instance within the mid-tier category across general compute and memory throughput routines. Stress-ng returned scores of 1,440.69 for single-core and 15,219.95 for multi-core compute tests. In Geekbench suites, the c4.4xlarge posted a single-core score of 1,182.0 and a multi-core score of 7,354.0, displaying reliable throughput for compilation tasks (13,105.0) and ray tracing (13,175.0). Memory evaluations show uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 89.52 GB/sec alongside write speeds of 47.18 GB/sec. Application testing shows 6.16 million operations per second for Redis SET requests and 11.52 GB/sec in static web serving.

Hardware tradeoffs are primarily defined by the older Haswell-generation processor architecture and the absence of native AVX-512 extensions. The server maintains standard AVX, FMA, and AES cryptographic instructions, but modern machine learning tasks face constraints. In language model evaluations, prompt processing for a 7B parameter model fell into the lower quartile at 23.37 tokens per second, with text generation averaging 10.7 tokens per second. Resource density favors core allocation over large working datasets.

From an infrastructure perspective, the c4.4xlarge functions cost-effectively for legacy compute pipelines that do not depend on advanced vector extensions or local high-speed NVMe storage. Target deployments include batch data processing, distributed compilation clusters, web server fleets handling static content, and intermediate queuing services.
description: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor, powered by a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor. Featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 30.0 GB of system memory, it offers an allocation ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 25 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX and AES instruction support, and 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero local storage or GPU hardware. Performance metrics demonstrate consistent mid-range capability, scoring 15,674.33 in Passmark CPU testing and achieving 6.16 million Redis SET operations per second. While unsuited for heavy AI inference or memory-heavy databases due to architectural age and capacity boundaries, it remains functional and cost-effective for static web serving, software build pipelines, and multithreaded compute batch operations.

bullet_points: Sixteen dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor at 2.9 GHz
Thirty gigabytes of system memory providing a compute-optimized ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU
Baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps with dedicated EBS-only storage architecture
Reliable mid-tier multithreaded performance across Passmark and Stress-ng benchmarks
Suited for software compilation, batch processing, and medium-scale web serving tiers
